Subject: Residency & backup follow-up — HealthPort (post-demo)

Hi Ava — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can produce an actionable privacy addendum for procurement: 

1) Call summary (minutes):
- HealthPort requires EU data residency for production PII (customer names, PHI-related metadata).
- You are open to a warm-standby in US for DR provided there are controls on what leaves the primary region (logs, backups).
- Retention: default retention target discussed was 7 years for records containing PII (you said legal will confirm).

2) Specific items we promised to follow up on: 
- Can Redwood ensure that primary inference and primary KV/prefix caches remain in EU?
- How are backups handled (frequency, encryption, cross-region replication)?
- What logging scopes are replicated to the US warm-standby (access logs, trace IDs, full request payloads)?
- Key management: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for backups and cross-region replicas?

3) Next steps: 
- Can you confirm whether HealthPort requires that audit logs never leave the EU (even to be accessible by Redwood Ops)?
- Please attach the compliance questionnaire you mentioned so Neha and Ben can route answers.

I attached a short SOC2 summary and a data-retention matrix from our last customer with similar needs. Ben — looping you to keep this thread on the account. Neha — can you confirm which of the options below are feasible and any constraints?

Options we can support (high level):
- EU-primary with warm-standby US (asynchronous cross-region mirror) — backups encrypted; customer-managed keys supported; logs can be filtered before cross-region replication.
- EU-only (no replication) — available for Private deployments or dedicated reserved pools with network egress blocked.
- Cross-region replication for cold backups only (daily snapshots) with strict encryption and separate retention controls.

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (summary), data-retention-matrix.csv (example).

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up call with security/legal if helpful.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer\Redwood Inference

Thanks for the forward. Quick technical answers and recommended controls we can propose to HealthPort: 

1) Key management: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for storage volumes and snapshot encryption on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we support a KMS integration option where the customer supplies keys via KMS federation; full HSM-backed BYOK is available for Private installs.

2) Backups & snapshots: snapshots include full filesystem state by default (this would include any persisted request payloads if stored). Options:
- Option A (preferred for HealthPort): do not persist raw requests to disk in EU production. Use ephemeral KV caches for inference-only tokens and only persist anonymized metadata. Daily cold snapshots (EU), encrypted with customer key; cross-region copy to US is only for cold disaster copies and can be disabled.
- Option B: allow snapshot replication to US but use pre-replication filtering to strip prompt/response fields and replace sensitive payloads with hashed references.

3) Logs & telemetry: by default, access logs (IP, timestamp, request id) are stored in the same region. Traces may be forwarded to our global observability stack unless configured otherwise. We can offer an EU-only observability endpoint for HealthPort that ensures no PII or prompt text is forwarded outside the EU.

4) Failover behavior: warm-standby (asynchronous) RPO can be as low as 15 minutes for dedicated pools with cross-region streaming enabled; RTO depends on capacity reservations in target region — typical plan: RPO = 15m, RTO = 30–60m with pre-warmed reserved nodes. Cold snapshot restore (from daily backups) RPO = 24h, RTO = several hours.

5) Operational controls: we will provide a runbook (region-failover-diagram.png) and include a test plan for DR exercises. Any cross-region access to logs for Redwood Ops will require explicit allowlisting and can be audited; we can provide log slices with PII redacted.

Action items:
- Olga: confirm HealthPort's required retention window (they mentioned 7 years) so we can calculate costs/retention tiers.
- Ben: please confirm the pre-warm capacity options and pricing delta for RTO=30m.
- I'll draft suggested wording for the privacy addendum regarding BYOK, EU-only logging, and snapshot controls.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ava — thanks, HealthPort Security. Below is a consolidated answer from our security and ops teams and proposed next steps so procurement/legal have concrete items for the SOW/addendum: 

Consolidated answers (high level)
- BYOK: supported. For Hosted API we support KMS federation; for Dedicated and Private we can support customer-managed HSM keys for snapshot and storage encryption.
- Backups/snapshots: defaults are EU-only. Cross-region replication to US is optional and can be disabled. If enabled, we will perform pre-replication filtering to remove prompt/response fields or store only hashed references per your requirement.
- Logs/telemetry: EU-only observability endpoint available to prevent PII from leaving the EU. Aggregated metrics can be shared globally.
- Failover: warm-standby RPO as low as 15 minutes on Dedicated with reserved capacity; RTO dependent on pre-warmed nodes (typical 30–60m). Cold backup restores are longer (hours).

Attachments and links:
- SOC2_summary.pdf (attached)
- data-retention-matrix.csv (attached)
- region-failover-diagram.png (attached)
- Draft privacy addendum link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-HealthPort-Residency

Proposed next steps: 
1) HealthPort to confirm retention period required for PII (you mentioned ~7 years).
2) If BYOK is required: share preferred KMS provider and whether HSM-backed keys are required.
3) Legal/procurement: confirm any language you want for the privacy addendum; we can draft and aim to get a first pass to you in 3 business days after you confirm retention and KMS requirements.
4) Optional: schedule a 30-minute technical DR runbook review with our Ops lead (Ben) and Neha to walk through the failover diagram and the pre-replication filters.

Would Tuesday at 10am CET work for a 30-minute DR review? If not, propose an alternative.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
